title: Cart and order domain model
idea: The cart domain model separates what a shopper intends (Cart, CartItem) from what was agreed (Order, Payment), with Product and Inventory as shared catalog data.

analogy.text: A shopping list versus a till receipt. You scribble and cross out the list freely; the receipt freezes items and prices the moment you pay.
analogy.breaks: An Order still changes status; a receipt never does.

points: A Cart belongs to one user and holds at most one CartItem per SKU.
An Order copies the cart lines, so later cart edits never change it.
Inventory tracks units on hand and units reserved per SKU.
A Payment belongs to one Order and carries an idempotency key.

edges.label: has 0..*
edges.caption: A Cart owns its CartItems, at most one per SKU. Adding the same SKU again merges quantities.

edges.label: refers 1
edges.caption: A CartItem points at a Product by SKU and remembers the price the shopper saw.

edges.label: counts 1
edges.caption: Inventory counts units per Product SKU. The cart never touches it directly.

edges.label: copies 1..*
edges.caption: An Order copies the cart lines at checkout. The copy is immutable.

edges.label: has
edges.caption: OrderStatus is an enum. Page 4 turns it into a state machine.

edges.label: for 1
edges.caption: A Payment is for exactly one Order and must have a positive amount.

edges.label: prices
edges.caption: PricingRule objects compute discounts at checkout. Page 3 implements them.

code.title: The model in Java 17
code.caption: Records for values, classes where state changes. Invariants live in constructors; money is a long in paise.

walk.text: Two products priced in paise, and stock: five mugs, one T-shirt.
Adding the mug twice merges into one line with quantity three.
The Order copies the cart; a later cart edit leaves the order alone.
Three bad inputs are refused by constructors, each with its own message.
Product and CartItem are records; CartItem caps quantity at ten.
`add` merges by SKU, so the cap applies to the merged quantity.
Order keeps a frozen copy of lines and starts as PENDING_PAYMENT.

pitfalls: Do not let Order hold a reference to the live Cart; copy the lines.
Keep money as long minor units; double cannot store most decimal prices exactly.
Do not put stock counts on Product; stock changes far more often than catalog data.

quiz.q: What does the first rejected line of DomainModel print?
quiz.why: The cart already holds four mugs. `add` merges 4 + 9 = 13, and the CartItem constructor rejects anything above ten.

takeaway: Cart is editable intent; Order is a frozen copy with a status.

starters: Should the cart store the price the shopper saw at all?
Why is Inventory separate from Product?
How would I model product variants like size and colour?
